purpose: Inspect whether the three empirical QSTN profile cards produce interpretable, context-sensitive permission choices before held-out calibration.
scope: A 3 prototype by 3 scenario qualitative diagnostic. It is not a benchmark or a human-likeness claim.
selection_policy: Scenarios are selected only from questionnaire metadata and the request-tool-data semantic relationship. No participant-level response labels are read or used.
interpretation_guardrails: Inspect profile differentiation, permission persistence, and response to contextual mismatch descriptively.
Do not compare pilot answers to participant labels or report accuracy, F1, significance, or human-likeness.
Do not treat any individual pilot answer as a pass/fail criterion for a profile card.
Use the audit artifacts to review the exact rendered prompts and raw model responses before any held-out calibration run.

cells.selection_rationale: A routine request in which listening history directly supports creating a playlist from the user's most-played songs.
cells.question_content:
User request: Create a playlist titled "Weekend Chill" with my most played songs.
Tool: Apple Music
Data item requested: Music playing history

request_messages.content: You are simulating a survey participant. Answer only from the supplied empirical permission-response profile, participant background, and permission scenario. Do not invent personal facts or purposes.

Answer each AI-agent data-sharing permission question as this canonical empirical profile would. Apply the profile as a behavioral tendency; it is not a license to invent facts or motivations. Choose exactly one option.

Stable empirical permission-response profile:
This participant generally favors enduring permission grants rather than renewed consent. They are more willing to grant permission when the scenario appears to support the user's request than when it appears not to. Treat this as a tendency, not a hard rule, and do not invent a purpose or personal fact.

Additional participant background: Not supplied for this canonical prototype.

Permission scenario:
Imagine that you are the user who made this request.
User request: Create a playlist titled "Weekend Chill" with my most played songs.
Tool: Apple Music
Data item requested: Music playing history

What permission would you give this AI assistant to share this data item with this tool?

Options are: No, never share, No, but ask me next time, Yes, but ask me next time, Yes, always share
